name: Baazem
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: newly discovered Yukubenic language (Lovegren 2012 mention only); no published description exists

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Uebersee 93: 299-326. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section concerns Akum only (three level tones, no stress statement); Baazem ('Bazɨm') mentioned once, p. 322, citing Lovegren 2012:11 for sentence-final vowel lengthening in polar questions. Nothing on Baazem stress.

sources.citation: Essegbey, James. 2019. Review of Kempf 2017, Verbal Serialisation in Bezen (Southern Jukunoid). Linguistique et Langues Africaines 5. doi:10.4000/lla.506
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Baazem content; notes Kempf 2017 covers Bezen syllable structure, vowel harmony and tone.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria. 2018. Kuteb verbal extensions vs. Bezen verbal serialisation: a comparison. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 4: 31-53. doi:10.4000/lla.9938
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Baazem prosody; fn. 8 states 'there are only short sketches of Akum (Akumbu & Brye 2002; Kempf & Prischnegg in preparation) and Bazɨm (Lovegren 2012)' -- confirms Lovegren 2012 is the sole description.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria. 2014 [2013]. Remnants of a noun class system in Bezen (Southern-Jukunoid). Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online.
